identity_evidence.quote: We here describe the case of an 85-year-old man

attribution_limitations: The article calls the visual impairment late-onset, while the case history says the patient began experiencing a progressive loss of vision at age three, lost central vision at 70 and became completely blind at 80. The article does not define late-onset; it may refer to the late onset of blindness (the Discussion compares the patient with late-blind subjects). This is an ambiguity of the label, not a conflict over the onset age.

The results say the significant alpha-band complexity increases were in the posterior areas of the left hemisphere and the centro-posterior areas of the right hemisphere; the discussion says the centro-posterior areas of the left hemisphere and the posterior areas of the right hemisphere. Both name the midline frontal areas.

Figure 3 caption gives a critical |t| of 3.12 for the theta connectivity comparison, while the supplementary Figure S2 image prints a different theta connectivity threshold. Image-printed values are pixel content and are not used as a conflict side.
The Figure 5 caption gives a single critical |t| of 2.41, while the supplementary Figure S6 image prints band-specific thresholds.
The source twice writes VS (RS and VS periods, RS and VS conditions) where VH is used elsewhere; VS is not defined.

The Results sentence on modularity and the participation coefficient says the whole scalp networks and does not name a band. The Discussion links the modularity increase to the theta connectivity decrease and the Figure 4 caption presents every graph metric in the theta band, so both facts are recorded for the theta networks.

The sentence stating that delta and theta PSD were higher during the RS condition as compared to VH does not name an electrode; the preceding sentence names the Fz subplot and the next names the Cz electrode.

The scope of the sentences of the second hallucination paragraph (The visual hallucinations he had were binocular ..., fully aware of their unreal nature) is not stated: they may restate the history or describe the EEG hallucination period.
Complete blindness at the age of 80 years is stated, while the ophthalmologic examination says he could perceive light in both eyes; blindness is not defined in the source.
The results describe the theta-band PSD decrease as involving virtually the whole frontal area, while the discussion says PSD decreases in the midline frontal areas for delta and theta bands.

The discussion says the PSD increases in the midline posterior areas correspond at a cortical level to posteromedial cortical regions, thus including the precuneus, and cites earlier reports for MRI, gray matter volume and fMRI findings of this patient. These are interpretations or cited findings, not results of this EEG.

Black dots indicate electrodes showing a significantly higher PSD during the VH condition as compared to RS, white dots the opposite relationship. limitations: Single-patient case report of EEG during and without visual hallucinations; the EEG results are scalp-level and the authors state that EEG spatial resolution is low and no compelling evidence for specific brain regions is available.

The left and right hemisphere regions of the alpha-band complexity increase conflict between Results and Discussion and are kept review-only; the undefined label late-onset visual impairment is review-only as an ambiguity against the stated onset of progressive vision loss at age three.

Values printed inside images (figures and the supplementary PDF) are pixel content only; critical t-values from the Figure 3 and Figure 5 captions are review-only because the supplementary images print different thresholds.
The source writes VS where VH is used elsewhere; the printed wording is kept and not corrected.

The MRI exam, gray matter volume and fMRI findings of this patient are cited to an earlier report; only the statements made about this patient in this article are recorded, and the MRI result is not available here.

EEG acquisition settings (hardware, reference, impedance, sampling rate, software), preprocessing and data-handling parameters (analyzed and discarded durations, retained channels, epoch counts, choice of representative electrodes) are methods and are not recorded as patient facts; the recording duration and periods, artifacts, Results-stated retained clean data and critical t-values of this recording are recorded.

Hallucination sentences of the results paragraph after the lead sentence carry no per-fact time because the lead sentence is not part of each fact quote; the scope of the later hallucination paragraph is not stated.
Supplementary PDF (Figures S1 to S6, Tables S1 to S3) is typed separately in the supplement review; pixel descriptions of the five main figures are in the visual submission.
